findings.issue_text: Authorization bypass in UsersResource.searchForUser: removing the per-user canView filter without handling the empty-group-set case means query-only admins with no group permissions now receive the entire user list

Per-user view/manage grants are ignored in user searches since the per-user canView filter was removed and the GROUPS attribute only covers group membership, making individually-granted users invisible

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects authz resource IDs (groupResource.getId()) instead of group IDs (should likely be getName()), causing group-scoped user searches/counts to return zero users

groupResource.getId() is passed into hasPermission which calls findByName, mismatching resource name against resource id so per-group permission checks fail and fall through to the all-groups fallback
GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage on VIEW scope, so view-only admins can create/update groups and map roles

Removal of the canViewGlobal || short-circuit in GroupResource/GroupsResource may cause admins with view-users but no fine-grained grants to get an empty group list if V1 GroupPermissions.canView(GroupModel) doesn't include the global check
Incorrect javadoc on requireManageMembers referencing canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers

canManage() in GroupPermissionsV2 falls back to a permission check accepting either VIEW or MANAGE scope on the all-groups resource, allowing view-only admins to pass requireManage() — privilege escalation

searchForUser in UsersResource (and BruteForceUsersResource) removes the !auth.users().canView() guard and the .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) post-filter, so callers with no group view permissions (empty getGroupIdsWithViewPermission) get unfiltered user search results — user-data disclosure

In V1 UserPermissions.canViewByGroup(), getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) was replaced by canViewMembers(group) which only checks root.users().canView(), losing view access for admins granted manage-members but not the view role — functional regression

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects groupResource.getId() (authz resource internal ID) but hasPermission looks up resources by name using group IDs; if the resource ID differs from the group ID, group-scoped user filtering silently matches nothing

Removal of canViewGlobal fast path in GroupResource.getSubGroups causes per-group canView evaluation (findByName + full policy evaluation) on an unpaginated stream, creating an N+1 authz evaluation for global admins; same pattern in GroupsResource.getGroups

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission in GroupPermissionsV2 iterates all group resources and performs a full hasPermission authorization evaluation per group with no early-exit or batching, dominating user search latency
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission result is recomputed on every call (e.g., getUsersCount and searchForUser each recompute it) instead of being cached per session/request

hasPermission in GroupPermissionsV2 may create the type-level resource (getOrCreate) inside a read-only boolean permission check, causing writes during GET evaluation and potentially in hot per-group loops
hasPermission builds Arrays.asList and nested loops per call, adding constant overhead multiplied by the per-group loops (minor)

BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser and UsersResource.searchForUser removed the if (!auth.users().canView()) guard, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is now called unconditionally on every user search (negligible cost, noted for completeness)

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authorization resource UUIDs instead of group IDs (group ID is stored as resource name), causing restricted admins to get empty search results and a count of 0
hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() but uses it for resourceStore.findByName, looking up a resource by name using its own ID, which fails to find it

Removal of the in-memory canView post-filter on user search results relies solely on providers honoring the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute, potentially returning users restricted admins should not see

GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel) removed and getGroupsWithViewPermission() renamed to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), breaking public interface consumers without deprecation
UserPermissions.canManageDefault() and canViewDefault() removed from public class without deprecation, breaking external callers
ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes(...) removed from public static utility in server-spi-private without deprecation, breaking extensions

AdminPermissions.registerListener now evaluates feature state once at registration time instead of per-event, risking role/group permission cleanup never running if registration precedes feature profile resolution

GroupResource.getSubGroups drops the explicit global-view short-circuit, potentially causing realm admins with view-users but no FGAP grant to lose subgroup visibility if V1's canView lacks the global check

Removed per-user authorization filter (.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)) in UsersResource.searchForUserStream exposes all realm users to callers with no view permission, since the UserModel.GROUPS attribute is never set when groupIds is empty
Same authorization bypass in BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser due to removed per-user filter
User-level grants (VIEW/MANAGE on specific user resources in V2) that don't correspond to the group-based DB filter will leak or be dropped since per-user evaluation no longer happens on the stream
canManage() in GroupPermissionsV2 returns true for VIEW scope in addition to MANAGE, allowing view-only admins to pass requireManage() and create/modify groups

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects authorization resource IDs instead of backing group IDs, so the returned set won't match UserModel.GROUPS group IDs and the group-based user filter matches nothing

Potential NPE in GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission when groupId is null and the type-level resource doesn't exist: policyStore.findByResource is called with null resource and ResourcePermission construction NPEs

Listener registration timing for fine-grained authz events checks the feature flag at registration time, so if registerListener runs before the feature profile is resolved, cleanup listeners for RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent are never registered, leaving orphaned permission resources

No negative test that unprivileged users are excluded after removal of the post-search filter in UsersResource.java; the new code relies entirely on GROUPS session attribute filtering with no test verifying a user in no permitted group is excluded

No test validating the semantics of getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() return values; it returns authorization resource IDs while hasPermission looks up by name via findByName, so a mismatch could silently return zero users

Behavioral change in UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership (no longer delegating to canManage, ADMIN role shortcut removed) has no test coverage, including no tests for callers with the composite ADMIN realm-management role or the new canManageByGroup fallback
No test coverage for GroupPermissionsV2 management-method UnsupportedOperationExceptions; admin REST endpoints like GroupResource.getPermissions may produce a raw 500 under the V2 evaluator
canViewMembers scope widening in V1 GroupPermissions (now also accepts MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE, requireViewMembers rerouted) is untested with a caller holding only manage-members

AdminPermissions.registerListener feature-check move (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ checked at registration time instead of inside the listener) has no test covering event-driven permission cleanup under either feature state

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), granting access to callers holding only VIEW scope; should check only MANAGE (likely copy-paste from canView())

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() collects resource IDs instead of group IDs via granted.add(groupResource.getId()), causing group-scoped user search/count to match nothing; should use groupResource.getName()

Removal of per-user canView filter in UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser is a security regression; if getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns empty, full user list is returned to callers without view permission
Near-total duplication of getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() between V1 and V2; shared traversal should be extracted into the base class with an overridable scope predicate to prevent drift

GroupPermissionsV2 throws bare UnsupportedOperationException on GroupPermissionManagement surface methods (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, getPermissions), which is reachable via AdminPermissions.registerListener's GroupRemovedEvent path
AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource throws IllegalStateException on unknown resource types, closing the schema to extension by SPIs/custom resource types

UsersResource drops the usersEvaluator::canView filter, so an admin with only query-users permission and empty groupIds gets no filtering at all and searchForUserStream returns every user in the realm (full disclosure)

Relying solely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute makes enforcement dependent on the UserStorageProvider honoring it; providers that ignore it leak all users and break firstResult/maxResults pagination semantics

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), letting view-only admins perform group creation, updates, child-group creation, and role mapping — privilege escalation contradicting the documented contract
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authorization-store resource UUIDs instead of group IDs, so group-scoped user filtering never matches and admins see zero or all users

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() only evaluates the per-group resource when it exists and never falls back to the type-level all-groups resource, silently bypassing all-groups permissions once a per-group resource exists

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() only collects per-group resources via findByType, so type-level VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants on all groups produce no entries, causing inconsistent authorization between list and single-resource paths

GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException on isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled/resource/viewPermission etc., which are called from admin REST flows causing 500 errors for existing clients/UI
requireViewMembers in GroupPermissions no longer honors manage-only admins (previously returned true when users().canManage() without canView()), a behavior change not covered by tests

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: canManage() in GroupPermissionsV2 returns true for VIEW scope in addition to MANAGE, allowing view-only admins to pass requireManage() and create/modify groups
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate flags that GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() incorrectly returns true for users with VIEW scope as well as MANAGE, allowing view-only admins to pass manage checks and modify groups. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment: canManage() should only accept MANAGE, while canView() can accept VIEW or MANAGE.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects groupResource.getId() (authz resource internal ID) but hasPermission looks up resources by name using group IDs; if the resource ID differs from the group ID, group-scoped user filtering silently matches nothing
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Yes. Both describe the same core bug: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the authz resource internal ID (groupResource.getId()) both for permission checks and for returning/collecting granted IDs, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as the underlying group ID). This ID-vs-name mismatch means per-group VIEW/MANAGE member permissions won’t produce the expected group IDs for later filtering/counting, potentially resulting in empty/incorrect matches (and effectively only working at the type-level resource).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization bypass in UsersResource.searchForUser: removing the per-user canView filter without handling the empty-group-set case means query-only admins with no group permissions now receive the entire user list

adjudication.rationale: In UsersResource.searchForUser, the diff removes the explicit per-user authorization filter: `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` is replaced with an unfiltered `searchForUserStream(...)` passed straight to `toRepresentation(...)`. The only remaining restriction is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` *only when* `groupIds` is non-empty. For a query-only admin with no group view permissions, `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` can be empty, so no session attribute is set and the unfiltered user search results are returned. Previously, even with an empty group set, the `usersEvaluator::canView` filter would prevent returning users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-user view/manage grants are ignored in user searches since the per-user canView filter was removed and the GROUPS attribute only covers group membership, making individually-granted users invisible

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `usersEvaluator::canView` filter in `UsersResource.searchForUser` (and similar in `BruteForceUsersResource`), but the stated consequence (“individually-granted users become invisible because only GROUPS membership is used”) is not supported by what’s shown. The new code only sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `groupIds` is non-empty; when it’s empty, no GROUPS restriction is applied at all. That change would not make per-user-granted users *invisible*; if anything, removing the per-user `canView` filter would more plausibly risk returning *more* users than allowed (depending on what `searchForUserStream` does), which is the opposite of the finding’s claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects authz resource IDs (groupResource.getId()) instead of group IDs (should likely be getName()), causing group-scoped user searches/counts to return zero users

groupResource.getId() is passed into hasPermission which calls findByName, mismatching resource name against resource id so per-group permission checks fail and fall through to the all-groups fallback

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the callback passes `groupResource.getId()` into `hasPermission(...)`. But `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, i.e., it expects a *resource name* (which per `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()` is the Keycloak group ID used as the resource name), not the authorization resource’s internal `id`. Passing the resource internal ID will typically make `findByName` return null, causing evaluation to fall back to the generic `GROUPS` resource-type resource and potentially miss per-group permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage on VIEW scope, so view-only admins can create/update groups and map roles

Removal of the canViewGlobal || short-circuit in GroupResource/GroupsResource may cause admins with view-users but no fine-grained grants to get an empty group list if V1 GroupPermissions.canView(GroupModel) doesn't include the global check

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show replacing `canViewGlobal || canView(g)` with `filter(auth.groups()::canView)` in `GroupResource`/`GroupsResource`, but the finding’s asserted impact (“admins with view-users … get an empty group list”) depends on whether V1 `GroupPermissions.canView(GroupModel)` lacks a global-role short-circuit. That method’s implementation is not shown/changed in this diff, and the updated `GroupPermissionEvaluator` Javadoc explicitly states `canView(GroupModel)` should return true for `MANAGE_USERS`/`VIEW_USERS` roles (i.e., a global check). So the claimed behavior is not verifiable from the diff and is presented conditionally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Incorrect javadoc on requireManageMembers referencing canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionEvaluator`, the Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` says it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` is false, but the method name implies it should correspond to `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. This is a verifiable documentation mismatch in the diff (comment above `requireManageMembers`). It does not affect runtime behavior but is a concrete review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canManage() in GroupPermissionsV2 falls back to a permission check accepting either VIEW or MANAGE scope on the all-groups resource, allowing view-only admins to pass requireManage() — privilege escalation

searchForUser in UsersResource (and BruteForceUsersResource) removes the !auth.users().canView() guard and the .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) post-filter, so callers with no group view permissions (empty getGroupIdsWithViewPermission) get unfiltered user search results — user-data disclosure

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser`, the diff removes the explicit post-filter `...searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now passes the raw `searchForUserStream(...)` into `toRepresentation(...)` without any visible per-user permission check in this hunk. If `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns empty (and thus no `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute is set), the search call is no longer constrained here and may return users the caller cannot view, which is a potential data disclosure. Note: the finding’s claim about removing a `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` in `BruteForceUsersResource` is incorrect (there was no such filter there), but the `UsersResource` part is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In V1 UserPermissions.canViewByGroup(), getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) was replaced by canViewMembers(group) which only checks root.users().canView(), losing view access for admins granted manage-members but not the view role — functional regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a regression where MANAGE_MEMBERS permission is ignored. In V1, `UserPermissions.canViewByGroup()` now calls `root.groups()::canViewMembers` (UserPermissions.java), and `GroupPermissions.canViewMembers(GroupModel)` explicitly checks permissions for both `VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE` **and** `MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE` (`return hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE);`, GroupPermissions.java). That matches the prior `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)` behavior, which also accepted `VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE` or `MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE`. Also, the shortcut `if (root.users().canView())` still covers admins with `MANAGE_USERS` because `UserPermissions.canView()` returns true for `MANAGE_USERS` or `VIEW_USERS` (UserPermissions.java).

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects groupResource.getId() (authz resource internal ID) but hasPermission looks up resources by name using group IDs; if the resource ID differs from the group ID, group-scoped user filtering silently matches nothing
matched_golden_ids: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both describe the same core bug: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the authz resource internal ID (groupResource.getId()) both for permission checks and for returning/collecting granted IDs, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as the underlying group ID). This ID-vs-name mismatch means per-group VIEW/MANAGE member permissions won’t produce the expected group IDs for later filtering/counting, potentially resulting in empty/incorrect matches (and effectively only working at the type-level resource).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of canViewGlobal fast path in GroupResource.getSubGroups causes per-group canView evaluation (findByName + full policy evaluation) on an unpaginated stream, creating an N+1 authz evaluation for global admins; same pattern in GroupsResource.getGroups

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `canViewGlobal` short-circuit in both `GroupResource.getSubGroups` and `GroupsResource.getGroups`, changing `.filter(g -> canViewGlobal || auth/groupsEvaluator.canView(g))` to `.filter(auth/groupsEvaluator::canView)`. In `GroupResource.getSubGroups`, the underlying stream is explicitly unpaginated (`group.getSubGroupsStream(..., -1, -1)`) and pagination happens after filtering (`paginatedStream(..., first, max)`), so this can introduce per-subgroup permission checks that were previously avoided when `canView()` was true. Whether those checks entail “findByName + full policy evaluation” is not provable from this diff (implementations may short-circuit on admin roles), and `GroupsResource.getGroups` uses already-paginated streams, so the “unpaginated N+1” claim doesn’t fully apply there. Still, the removed fast path is a concrete, diff-grounded performance concern rather than a functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission in GroupPermissionsV2 iterates all group resources and performs a full hasPermission authorization evaluation per group with no early-exit or batching, dominating user search latency

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code iterates *all* group resources via `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and for each resource calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS)`, which performs a full `root.evaluatePermission(...)` authorization evaluation. There is no batching/caching and no early-exit (it must compute the full set), so for realms with many groups this can be an O(#groups × authz-eval) hot path. The diff also changes user search to always call `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and set `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when non-empty (e.g., `UsersResource#searchForUser` and `BruteForceUsersResource#searchForUser`), making this performance cost more likely to impact user search latency. This is a performance/architecture concern, not a correctness defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission result is recomputed on every call (e.g., getUsersCount and searchForUser each recompute it) instead of being cached per session/request

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` being called directly from multiple entrypoints (e.g., `UsersResource#getUsersCount` and `UsersResource#searchForUser`, plus `BruteForceUsersResource#searchForUser`). The implementation (notably `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`) iterates over all group resources via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and evaluates permissions per group, with no caching layer visible in the diff. That makes the finding (recomputed on each call) accurate, but it’s a performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission in GroupPermissionsV2 may create the type-level resource (getOrCreate) inside a read-only boolean permission check, causing writes during GET evaluation and potentially in hot per-group loops

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#hasPermission` the diff shows only reads against `resourceStore`/`policyStore` and a fallback to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. There is no call to `getOrCreateResource` (or any explicit create/write) in this method in the provided diff, so the claim that a boolean permission check "may create" resources and cause writes during GET evaluation is not verifiable from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission builds Arrays.asList and nested loops per call, adding constant overhead multiplied by the per-group loops (minor)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes)`, the code creates `List<String> expectedScopes = Arrays.asList(scopes);` and then does nested loops over `permissions` and `permission.getScopes()`, calling `expectedScopes.contains(scope)` each time. Additionally, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` iterates all group resources and calls `hasPermission(...)` per group, multiplying this per-call constant overhead. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/efficiency concern but not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser and UsersResource.searchForUser removed the if (!auth.users().canView()) guard, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is now called unconditionally on every user search (negligible cost, noted for completeness)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the guard `if (!auth.users().canView())` was removed and `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is now invoked unconditionally in both `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` and `UsersResource.searchForUser`. However, the finding only notes a “negligible cost” and does not identify any concrete defect or actionable review issue introduced by the change; it’s essentially a trivial/perf nit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authorization resource UUIDs instead of group IDs (group ID is stored as resource name), causing restricted admins to get empty search results and a count of 0

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code iterates `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. It also calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, and `hasPermission` looks up a resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. This is inconsistent: `getId()` is the authz Resource UUID, while `findByName` expects the resource *name* (which for group resources is the Keycloak group id, per `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup` returning `group.getId()`). Consequently, the method returns authz resource UUIDs (or evaluates permissions against the wrong resource), which won’t match actual Keycloak group IDs expected by callers (e.g., `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource` setting `UserModel.GROUPS`), leading to empty/incorrect user search/count results for restricted admins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() but uses it for resourceStore.findByName, looking up a resource by name using its own ID, which fails to find it

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`, it iterates `resourceStore.findByType(..., groupResource -> { if (hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)) ... })`. But `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` treats that argument as a *group id / resource name* and calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Passing `groupResource.getId()` (the authorization Resource's internal id) into `findByName` is very likely wrong; it should use the resource name (e.g., `groupResource.getName()`, which per `AdminPermissionsSchema#getOrCreateResource` is based on the group id). As written, the lookup will often miss, falling back to the resource-type (“all-groups”) resource and producing incorrect per-group permission results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of the in-memory canView post-filter on user search results relies solely on providers honoring the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute, potentially returning users restricted admins should not see

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` the stream is no longer post-filtered with `usersEvaluator::canView` (removed `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`), and instead the code now only sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` based on `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`. That does shift enforcement toward `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` honoring the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute to constrain results. The diff does not show that `searchForUserStream` (or `toRepresentation(...)`) will always enforce visibility for all user storage providers/custom providers, so this is a concrete security/architecture concern introduced by the change, but not a defect that can be proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel) removed and getGroupsWithViewPermission() renamed to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), breaking public interface consumers without deprecation

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GroupPermissionEvaluator` had `boolean getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel group)` removed entirely and `Set<String> getGroupsWithViewPermission()` renamed to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (with signature/name change) without any `@Deprecated` bridge/default method. While in-repo call sites were updated (e.g., `UsersResource` and `GroupPermissions`), this is a source/binary incompatible public interface change that can break external consumers of the SPI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UserPermissions.canManageDefault() and canViewDefault() removed from public class without deprecation, breaking external callers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove two previously public methods from `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissions.java`: `public boolean canManageDefault()` and `public boolean canViewDefault()` (the latter existed at the bottom of the class and is removed as well). There is no `@Deprecated` annotation or replacement shim added for these methods in this diff, so any downstream code compiling against these public methods would break at compile time. The diff alone can’t prove that external callers exist, but the API removal itself is real and potentially compatibility-impacting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes(...) removed from public static utility in server-spi-private without deprecation, breaking extensions

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly deletes the public static utility method `ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes(...)` from `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/ModelToRepresentation.java` with no replacement wrapper or deprecation period. Any external code (including extensions) compiled against that method will fail to compile after this change. This is an API compatibility concern rather than an in-product runtime defect, but it is directly grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions.registerListener now evaluates feature state once at registration time instead of per-event, risking role/group permission cleanup never running if registration precedes feature profile resolution

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `registerListener` now guards registration with `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...))` instead of checking the flag on every event. While this changes behavior if feature flags could flip after registration, the diff provides no evidence that feature state is resolved later or is mutable at runtime, so the claimed risk (“cleanup never running if registration precedes profile resolution”) is not verifiable from the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupResource.getSubGroups drops the explicit global-view short-circuit, potentially causing realm admins with view-users but no FGAP grant to lose subgroup visibility if V1's canView lacks the global check

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupResource.getSubGroups`, the filter changed from `canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g)` to `auth.groups()::canView`. This only causes loss of visibility if `canView(GroupModel)` does *not* already include the global-role check. The diff’s own updated `GroupPermissionEvaluator` Javadoc explicitly states `canView(GroupModel)` should return true for callers with `MANAGE_USERS`/`VIEW_USERS` roles (i.e., the “global” case), and `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)` clearly implements that short-circuit. The diff does not show any change removing the global short-circuit from V1 `GroupPermissions.canView(GroupModel)`, so the claimed behavior regression is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed per-user authorization filter (.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)) in UsersResource.searchForUserStream exposes all realm users to callers with no view permission, since the UserModel.GROUPS attribute is never set when groupIds is empty

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the explicit per-user permission filter in `UsersResource.searchForUser` (`.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`), and it now relies on setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` only when `groupIds` is non-empty. If `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set for a caller that lacks global view (e.g., no group-based grants found), the session attribute is not set at all. However, the finding’s claim that this definitively “exposes all realm users” cannot be verified from the diff alone because the behavior of `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` and/or `toRepresentation(...)` regarding permission filtering is not shown. Still, it is a concrete, diff-grounded security/correctness concern created by removing the explicit filter while not setting an explicit empty restriction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same authorization bypass in BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser due to removed per-user filter

adjudication.rationale: In BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser/searchForUser(), the diff does not remove any per-user permission filter because there wasn’t one there to begin with: both before and after it directly calls session.users().searchForUserStream(...) and passes the result to toRepresentation(...) without a .filter(usersEvaluator::canView). The only changes in that method are switching from getGroupsWithViewPermission() to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() and removing the surrounding if (!auth.users().canView()) block (while still only setting the session attribute when the returned set is non-empty). The finding’s stated cause (“removed per-user filter”) is not supported by this diff for BruteForceUsersResource.

adjudication_records.issue_text: User-level grants (VIEW/MANAGE on specific user resources in V2) that don't correspond to the group-based DB filter will leak or be dropped since per-user evaluation no longer happens on the stream

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)`, the diff removes the per-user permission filter (`.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`) and now directly streams `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` into `toRepresentation(...)` (which in this diff does not reintroduce an equivalent filter). Previously, even when the DB-side group restriction (`session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)`) was absent/empty, per-user evaluation still prevented unauthorized users from appearing in search results. Now results are effectively constrained only by the optional `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute, which is derived from `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`. Any V2 grants that allow viewing/managing a specific user (or any case where `canQuery()` allows access to the endpoint but `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is empty) will not be enforced at the stream level, causing authorized-per-user users to be dropped from search and/or unauthorized users to be returned. The same pattern appears in `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canManage() in GroupPermissionsV2 returns true for VIEW scope in addition to MANAGE, allowing view-only admins to pass requireManage() and create/modify groups
matched_golden_ids: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() incorrectly returns true for users with VIEW scope as well as MANAGE, allowing view-only admins to pass manage checks and modify groups. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment: canManage() should only accept MANAGE, while canView() can accept VIEW or MANAGE.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects authorization resource IDs instead of backing group IDs, so the returned set won't match UserModel.GROUPS group IDs and the group-based user filter matches nothing

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`, the code iterates group resources via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set, and also calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`. However, `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` looks up a resource by *name* (`resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`), and `AdminPermissionsSchema#resolveGroup` uses the backing `GroupModel` id as the resource name. This indicates the group resource's **name** is the groupId, while `Resource#getId()` is the authorization-store internal id. Returning/using `groupResource.getId()` therefore won’t match real group IDs expected by `UserModel.GROUPS` (set in `UsersResource` / `BruteForceUsersResource`), and permission checks for per-group resources will also fail because `findByName` is given an authz resource id instead of the group id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Potential NPE in GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission when groupId is null and the type-level resource doesn't exist: policyStore.findByResource is called with null resource and ResourcePermission construction NPEs

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, a null groupId is explicitly handled by skipping findByName and then assigning `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` before calling `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and constructing `new ResourcePermission(resource, ...)`. The diff does not show any path where `policyStore.findByResource` is called with a null `resource` unless `getResourceTypeResource` itself returns null, which is not evidenced in this diff. So the finding’s described NPE path is not verifiable from the shown changes and misreads the null-handling present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Listener registration timing for fine-grained authz events checks the feature flag at registration time, so if registerListener runs before the feature profile is resolved, cleanup listeners for RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent are never registered, leaving orphaned permission resources

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change AdminPermissions.registerListener to gate listener registration on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...) (previously the listener was always registered and the feature flag was checked inside onEvent). However, the finding’s core claim—"registerListener runs before the feature profile is resolved" leading to missing registration and orphaned resources—cannot be verified from this PR diff. The diff shows no evidence that feature resolution is deferred or that the feature could become enabled after registerListener runs; without that, the described timing bug is speculative rather than a diff-grounded defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No negative test that unprivileged users are excluded after removal of the post-search filter in UsersResource.java; the new code relies entirely on GROUPS session attribute filtering with no test verifying a user in no permitted group is excluded

adjudication.rationale:
In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` the diff removes the explicit post-search permission filter (`.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`) and now passes the raw `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` into `toRepresentation(...)`, while only optionally setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` based on `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`.

Although a new test (`GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`) asserts an initially unprivileged admin sees no users at all, the diff does not add a negative test that specifically validates that, once some group IDs are permitted, users *outside* those permitted groups are still excluded (i.e., protection against over-inclusion after removing the explicit stream filter). Given the behavioral change, this is a concrete missing-test concern tied to the changed logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test validating the semantics of getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() return values; it returns authorization resource IDs while hasPermission looks up by name via findByName, so a mismatch could silently return zero users

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, it iterates `resourceStore.findByType(..., groupResource -> ...)` and passes `groupResource.getId()` into `hasPermission(...)`, but `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` then does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. `findByName` expects the resource *name* (likely the group id/name), not the resource's internal id/UUID. This mismatch can prevent locating per-group resources, causing `hasPermission` to fall back to the all-groups resource-type check and potentially return `false` for all groups, which would in turn make `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` return an empty set and user searches return zero users. The diff shows no direct correction or test explicitly covering this ID-vs-name lookup path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change in UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership (no longer delegating to canManage, ADMIN role shortcut removed) has no test coverage, including no tests for callers with the composite ADMIN realm-management role or the new canManageByGroup fallback

adjudication.rationale:
The diff changes authorization logic in `UserPermissionsV2`:
- Removes `AdminRoles.ADMIN` from the short-circuit in `canView(UserModel)`/`canManage(UserModel)` (e.g. `if (root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.ADMIN, ...)` -> `if (root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, ...)`) and changes `canMapRoles`/`canManageGroupMembership` to no longer delegate to `canManage(user)` and to add `|| canManageByGroup(user)` fallback (`UserPermissionsV2.java` hunk).
The newly added tests (`GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`) cover viewing/managing users via group membership for `canViewByGroup`/`canManageByGroup` (e.g. update user after granting `MANAGE_MEMBERS`), and manage group membership via user scope `MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP`, but they do not exercise the specific changed methods `canMapRoles` or `canManageGroupMembership` under the new fallback path, nor do they create a caller with the composite/admin role that was removed from the shortcut checks. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a proven functional break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for GroupPermissionsV2 management-method UnsupportedOperationExceptions; admin REST endpoints like GroupResource.getPermissions may produce a raw 500 under the V2 evaluator

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `GroupPermissionsV2` and wires it in via `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()`, but many management-style methods in `GroupPermissionsV2` (e.g., `setPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `resource`, `managePermission`, etc.) now unconditionally `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. The new/updated tests focus on scope evaluation (e.g., `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`) and do not exercise or assert safe handling of these UnsupportedOperationException paths. Whether specific admin REST endpoints (e.g., a hypothetical `GroupResource.getPermissions`) will call these methods and yield a 500 is not shown in this diff, but the risk introduced by wiring an implementation that throws at runtime without coverage/guards is concrete and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canViewMembers scope widening in V1 GroupPermissions (now also accepts MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE, requireViewMembers rerouted) is untested with a caller holding only manage-members

adjudication.rationale: The diff does widen V1 `GroupPermissions.canViewMembers(GroupModel)` from `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` to `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` and changes `requireViewMembers` to delegate to `canViewMembers` (previously it used `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)`). While a new integration test `testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers` exercises MANAGE_MEMBERS implying view-by-membership, it likely targets the new V2 permissions path (new `GroupPermissionsV2`, `AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`). The diff shows no explicit test that the V1 `GroupPermissions` behavior (scopes widening + reroute) works for a caller granted only MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE, so the finding is a specific, diff-grounded coverage gap rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions.registerListener feature-check move (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ checked at registration time instead of inside the listener) has no test covering event-driven permission cleanup under either feature state

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes AdminPermissions.registerListener to gate listener registration on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) at registration time, instead of checking inside onEvent (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). This is a behavioral change for event-driven cleanup (handling RoleRemovedEvent / GroupRemovedEvent calling management(...).users().setPermissionsEnabled(false) and groups().setPermissionsEnabled(...)). The added tests (e.g., GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest) cover permission evaluation flows but do not exercise these provider events under either feature-enabled or feature-disabled states, so there is no diff-visible test coverage for this event-driven cleanup behavior after the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), granting access to callers holding only VIEW scope; should check only MANAGE (likely copy-paste from canView())

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2` (services/.../GroupPermissionsV2.java), `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. The helper `hasPermission(...)` returns true if *any* of the provided scopes are present in evaluated permissions, so a caller with only the `VIEW` scope on the “all-groups” resource type would be treated as having manage capability. This is inconsistent with `canManage(GroupModel group)`, which checks only `MANAGE`, and would allow callers with view-only permissions to pass global manage checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() collects resource IDs instead of group IDs via granted.add(groupResource.getId()), causing group-scoped user search/count to match nothing; should use groupResource.getName()

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the loop iterates `resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> ...)` and on grant does `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. However this method is explicitly used as *group IDs* in `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource` (stored in `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` and passed to `session.users().getUsersCount(..., auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission())`). `groupResource.getId()` is the authz Resource internal id, not the group id/name used elsewhere (and `hasPermission` itself looks up by `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, implying the "identifier" should be the resource name, which for groups is resolved to `group.getId()` in `AdminPermissionsSchema#resolveGroup`). This mismatch means group-specific permissions won’t translate into the correct group-id set for user search/count (likely yielding empty/mis-scoped results unless an all-groups permission exists). Using `groupResource.getName()` (resource name == group id) would align with the intended semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of per-user canView filter in UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser is a security regression; if getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns empty, full user list is returned to callers without view permission

adjudication.rationale: In both UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser, the diff removes the per-user permission filter (`.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`) and now always returns `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` results directly to `toRepresentation(...)`. The only added restriction is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. If that set is empty for a caller who also lacks global user view (e.g., no group-level view-members permissions), the code applies no restriction at all in this method, unlike before. That makes the reported “full user list may be returned” a plausible and diff-grounded security regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Near-total duplication of getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() between V1 and V2; shared traversal should be extracted into the base class with an overridable scope predicate to prevent drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two implementations of the same high-level routine: `GroupPermissions#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (in `GroupPermissions`) and an override in the new `GroupPermissionsV2`. Both perform the same control-flow and traversal: (1) early-return empty set if `root.users().canView()`, (2) early-return if `!root.isAdminSameRealm()`, (3) early-return if `root.realmResourceServer()` is null, (4) iterate `resourceStore.findByType(...)` over group resources and add IDs that pass a permission check. The main difference is only the permission-check details (`hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` vs `hasPermission(groupId, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW_MEMBERS, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_MEMBERS)`). This is a real maintainability/architecture issue introduced by the change (risk of drift between V1 and V2), not a functional defect evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2 throws bare UnsupportedOperationException on GroupPermissionManagement surface methods (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, getPermissions), which is reachable via AdminPermissions.registerListener's GroupRemovedEvent path

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` is overridden to return `new GroupPermissionsV2(...)` (services/.../MgmtPermissionsV2.java). `GroupPermissionsV2` extends `GroupPermissions` (which implements the management surface) but overrides multiple management methods to throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, including `setPermissionsEnabled(GroupModel, boolean)` and `isPermissionsEnabled(GroupModel)` (services/.../GroupPermissionsV2.java). Meanwhile, `AdminPermissions.registerListener` registers a listener (when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled) that, on `GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent`, calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false)` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). With V2 enabled, that call would dispatch to `GroupPermissionsV2#setPermissionsEnabled` and throw at runtime during group removal handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource throws IllegalStateException on unknown resource types, closing the schema to extension by SPIs/custom resource types

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(...) to use a switch with a default branch that throws IllegalStateException when resourceType is not one of CLIENTS/GROUPS/USERS (see the new `default -> throw new IllegalStateException(...)`). This is a real behavior/compatibility change for any caller that might pass other resource types (e.g., via SPI/custom types), and it makes the schema explicitly closed to unknown types rather than allowing any fallback behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsersResource drops the usersEvaluator::canView filter, so an admin with only query-users permission and empty groupIds gets no filtering at all and searchForUserStream returns every user in the realm (full disclosure)

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)`, the diff removes the explicit per-user permission filter: `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` is replaced by an unfiltered `searchForUserStream(...)` passed directly into `toRepresentation(...)`. The only remaining restriction in this method is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty; if that set is empty for a caller who is not allowed global view (e.g., query-only with no group member-view grants), the method no longer applies any `canView` filtering at this layer and will return whatever `searchForUserStream` returns. The diff does not show `toRepresentation(...)` adding an equivalent permission check, and the fact the old code filtered before calling it suggests it likely does not enforce `canView` itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Relying solely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute makes enforcement dependent on the UserStorageProvider honoring it; providers that ignore it leak all users and break firstResult/maxResults pagination semantics

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` the diff removes the explicit per-user permission filter (`.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`) and now returns `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` directly, only optionally setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `groupIds` is non-empty. If the caller cannot globally view users and `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set (e.g., no granted groups / provider not configured / not same realm), the code does not set any restricting attribute and performs an unrestricted search, which would expose users that `usersEvaluator::canView` would previously have filtered out. This change makes correctness/security depend on the underlying user provider honoring the session attribute and on `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` distinguishing “no restriction” vs “no permission”, which it does not (empty set is used in multiple cases).

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), letting view-only admins perform group creation, updates, child-group creation, and role mapping — privilege escalation contradicting the documented contract

adjudication.rationale: In the new `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it treats the `VIEW` scope on the *group resource type* (the “all-groups” fallback) as sufficient for “manage” at the global level. Since `requireManage()` delegates to `canManage()`, any code path that gates mutating group operations on the global check (e.g., creating top-level groups) would be incorrectly authorized by a view-only permission. This is diff-verifiable from `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` and `requireManage()` behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authorization-store resource UUIDs instead of group IDs, so group-scoped user filtering never matches and admins see zero or all users

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code iterates authz resources (`resourceStore.findByType(..., groupResource -> ...)`) and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set (`granted.add(groupResource.getId())`). In Keycloak authz, `Resource#getId()` is the authorization-store resource UUID, while the actual group identifier is the group model ID which is used as the resource *name* (see `AdminPermissionsSchema#resolveGroup()` returning `group.getId()` and `getOrCreateResource(...)` using that as the resolved name). Callers (`UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource`) put this set into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`, which is intended to contain real group IDs. Returning authz resource UUIDs will therefore not match group membership filtering semantics, leading to incorrect user search/count results for group-scoped visibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() only evaluates the per-group resource when it exists and never falls back to the type-level all-groups resource, silently bypassing all-groups permissions once a per-group resource exists

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes)`, when `groupId != null` it first resolves a per-group resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. If that resource exists, the method evaluates permissions only against that per-group `Resource` and never additionally evaluates the type-level `AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE` resource (the “all-groups” fallback). The fallback to the type-level resource is only executed when the per-group resource is `null`. Therefore, if an all-groups permission grants e.g. `VIEW`/`MANAGE`, but a per-group resource exists (perhaps created for other policies) and does not grant those scopes to the caller, `hasPermission` will return false—effectively bypassing global all-groups permissions once a per-group resource exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() only collects per-group resources via findByType, so type-level VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants on all groups produce no entries, causing inconsistent authorization between list and single-resource paths

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the granted set is built by iterating only existing per-group resources via resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). For each found resource it calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS), which looks up a Resource by name=groupId and, if it exists, evaluates only that resource’s permissions (no fallback). Type-level “all-groups” permissions are only considered in hasPermission() when the per-group resource is missing (fallback to getResourceTypeResource), but getGroupIdsWithViewPermission never evaluates anything if there are no per-group resources, and it also won’t consider type-level grants when per-group resources exist but have no policies. This creates inconsistent behavior vs single-group checks like canViewMembers(group), which *do* fall back to the type-level resource when a per-group resource is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException on isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled/resource/viewPermission etc., which are called from admin REST flows causing 500 errors for existing clients/UI

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `GroupPermissionsV2` (used by `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()`), and this class overrides multiple `GroupPermissionManager` methods (e.g., `setPermissionsEnabled`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `viewPermission`, etc.) to throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. The diff also shows `AdminPermissions.registerListener` invoking `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(...)` on `GroupRemovedEvent` and `RoleRemovedEvent`. If the V2 permission management path uses `MgmtPermissionsV2` (as implied by the added override), those listener invocations would now hit `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` and throw at runtime, likely resulting in internal errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: requireViewMembers in GroupPermissions no longer honors manage-only admins (previously returned true when users().canManage() without canView()), a behavior change not covered by tests

adjudication.rationale: While `GroupPermissions.requireViewMembers` was changed to call `canViewMembers(group)` instead of the removed `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)`, the claimed regression (“manage-only admins where `users().canManage()` is true but `users().canView()` is false”) is not supported by the diff. In `UserPermissions`, `canView()` is satisfied by either VIEW or MANAGE scope/roles (`root.hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_USERS, VIEW_USERS)` or permission scopes `VIEW`/`MANAGE`), so having manage implies view. Therefore removing the explicit `root.users().canManage()` check from the old helper does not create a new class of admins who can manage but cannot view members. The finding’s asserted behavior change cannot be verified from the shown code.
